executive_summary.headline: Macro and shipping chokepoints both weakening; Hormuz transits collapsed 94% year-on-year while EU gas prices remain elevated.
executive_summary.next_step: Within 48 hours, confirm whether the Hormuz transit collapse is temporary (weather, seasonal) or structural; cross-check with shipping brokers on rerouting costs and timeline impact to your container schedules.
executive_summary.context: The macro pillar moved to AMBER today as EU outlook weakened, while world signals show critical pressure: Strait of Hormuz transits down 94% versus a year ago and Bab el-Mandeb down 34%, forcing longer routing around Africa. Combined with Rhine levels at 26 cm (below 40 cm threshold) and EU natural gas 131% above September baseline, input costs and logistics times face material headwind. These route and energy constraints are now the primary drivers of overall AMBER status.
